first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence suggests shorter onboarding improves time-to-value while in-product activation messaging improves first meaningful action. Verify both records and run a guarded simplification test, measuring qualified activation, downstream conversion, and retention rather than completion alone. Avoid promotional pricing because prior gains materially reduced 30-day retention.

mid.rationale: Run a controlled onboarding simplification experiment, prioritizing the directly observed completion and time-to-value decline while leveraging evidence of improved 30-day retention. Track qualified activation, first meaningful action, pipeline or paid conversion, and 30-day retention—not completion alone. Activation messaging is a credible fallback, but simplifying onboarding addresses both the completion problem and the activation bottleneck with stronger retention evidence. Do not use promotional pricing because its acquisition lift materially harmed retention.

final2.rationale: Run a tightly targeted, time-limited offer for demonstrably price-sensitive SMB accounts as a direct response to the competitor’s deeper cut and doubled churn conversations. Use retention and qualified-revenue guardrails: monitor 30-day retention, gross revenue retention, conversion quality, expansion, and contribution margin, with automatic rollback if retention deteriorates. Prior evidence supports acquisition and revenue lift but shows material 30-day retention harm, so this should not become a broad pricing strategy.
